3 of which Nosler and Barnes are somewhat useless since getting the gun powders in their recipes is kinda impossible.

Pretty much just Vihtavuori and Norma powders here (Finland) and even Norma is harder to get and might require trip to Sweden.

So using Finnish reloading book written by Esa Paananen. Which has the right powders and nice selection of bullets. Also using Vihtavuori Android app. Bullet manufacturers might have reloading data on their websites too.

I have 4 manuals, two are fairly old and two are newer. They are a product of their time, one has a single page of 223rem loads compared to another that has 6 pages. Plus, the old manuals load a bit hotter than the new, risk adverse, manuals. It's part of the study needed to advance to the point where the manual is a guide rather than a recipe.

I have four (Nosler, Sierra, Hornady and Speer), which covers the bullets I mainly load up.

I use the Interwebz for the less common stuff like Lasercast lead bullets.

In fact, I do a lot of cross referencing on the web.
From digital manuals to hard books, maybe 15 sources.

I have a bunch of PDFs, but only one physical book, which is ancient, Speer Reloading Number Ten.

I try to cross reference a few manuals whenever possible, along with the (bullet/powder) manufacturer's load data.

Lots of times I will find data that doesn't jive across publishers, especially when it comes to max loads. I find manufacturer load data to be really lawyerly, typically the max load sits somewhere in the middle of the real range in those instances...
